quotes.text: Bacs Direct Debit transactions have a default limit of 10,000 GBP each.
You can’t submit evidence or counter a Bacs Direct Debit dispute.
Custom API mandate collection requires Stripe approval.
The `checkout.session.completed` event confirms that the customer submitted and authorized the Checkout form. It doesn’t mean the asynchronous Bacs payment succeeded.
Custom branding typically takes 10 business days to become active.

old_evidence.text: BACS Direct Debit transactions have a limit of 100,000 GBP each.
Stripe users in the UK can accept Bacs Direct Debit payments from customers with a UK bank account.
Your business name is shown for new mandates created 5 business days after your request.

findings: Attempt 2 retains the accepted attempt 1 worker's complete numbered read proof for the four unchanged SHA-256-pinned files; appended ranges are this worker's own targeted numbered reads. The prior receipt and full review match their trusted attempt-2 hashes, as do all four evidence pins.

Debit-notification scope correction: both captures require notification when Bacs details are collected/confirmed and before each debit (old raw lines 127-136; new raw lines 298-302). May says Stripe sends those emails by default without naming an exception; November expressly excepts enterprise accounts with a custom service user number (SUN) from Stripe's default email sending, while self-sent notifications follow eligibility and approval (new raw lines 300-302). Current source line 29 and concept stripe-bacs-direct-debit line 45 state blanket Stripe auto-emailing and should be qualified by account context. Mandate/advance-debit notices are not payment-success receipts, as new raw lines 344-350 clarifies; do not infer that the SUN exception removes Bacs notification duties or suppresses every Stripe email.

Central Bacs behavior remains reusable, GBP bank debit against a customer's UK bank account, authorized by a Direct Debit Instruction mandate with sort code, account number, name, email and full address; access requires additional identity verification and is approval-gated (new raw lines 5-31, 73-80, 156-166; old raw lines 4-14, 78-80, 148-152). Confirmation is delayed, typically four business days for an existing mandate or up to seven with a new mandate; mandate acceptance and payment submission do not establish success (new raw lines 13-18, 259-296, 318-356; old raw lines 14, 102-125).

Material scope/limit change: May described UK Stripe accounts, outside-UK platforms acting for UK connected accounts, and 100,000 GBP per transaction plus 10,000 GBP weekly for new users (old raw lines 8-12, 58-65). November lists many supported merchant business countries, cross-border geographic coverage but still GB customer location and GBP presentment, and a default 10,000 GBP per-transaction limit with a separate 10,000 GBP weekly limit for new users that can increase; support can consider higher limits (new raw lines 9, 22-27, 65-85). Do not call Bacs globally UK-business-only or confuse the per-transaction default with the new-user weekly limit. The restricted/prohibited MCC table is newly detailed, with account review possible (new raw lines 27-63); it does not establish a particular account's approval.

New refund/dispute outcome boundaries expand older rules: the 180-day refund window, 3-4-business-day processing, separate-credit-not-reversal nature, indefinite indemnity/double-credit risk and pending refund after Charge success were already present (old raw lines 171-179; new raw lines 103-128). November adds explicit refund.failed and refund.updated status routing and says neither refund.created nor charge.refunded alone proves success or bank posting (new raw lines 130-134). November says one dispute per Bacs payment, no fixed bank-to-Stripe dispute receipt timing, no merchant evidence/counter/appeal, final bank decision and nonrefundable dispute fee; May already had indefinite filing, charge.dispute.created, deduction, final/nonappealable outcome (new raw lines 136-154; old raw lines 138-146).

Mandate detail is newly explicit: Checkout collects bank details/acceptance, Payment Element cannot create Bacs SetupIntents and Checkout setup mode is the stated alternative, while custom API mandate collection separately requires Stripe approval and an exact checkbox text/form content (new raw lines 156-184; old raw lines 66-76, 148-158). The Mandate object stores business, acceptance and reference; mandate.updated requires checking active status and cancellation blocks future debits (new raw lines 162-195; old raw lines 150-169). New Pay by Bank Recurring is a separate private-preview initial Pay by Bank payment plus Bacs mandate, not proof that ordinary Bacs confirmation is instant or that any account has preview access (new raw lines 197-208).

November separates payment processing from funds availability: for an existing mandate it describes typical customer debit T+2, PaymentIntent success T+3 21:00 UTC, and funds in Stripe T+4 00:00 UTC; for a new mandate it lists submission T+3, debit T+5, available T+7 (new raw lines 259-285; old raw lines 102-125). Checkout session.completed means submitted/authorized, while checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded or failed gives its later outcome; PaymentIntents use processing/succeeded/payment_failed (new raw lines 286-296). Checkout session expiration is 24 hours by default and configurable 30 minutes-24 hours, separate from Bacs processing; no distinct custom-integration authorization timeout is specified (new raw lines 354-358).

Connect and branding details changed: November says supported-location platforms can use destination charges with or without on_behalf_of, platform is settlement merchant when on_behalf_of omitted, and connected-account bacs_debit_payments capability is required when on_behalf_of is used (new raw lines 249-257). May separately described an outside-UK platform needing capability for its UK connected account and a UK-platform destination-charge exception (old raw lines 181-199); retain the dated difference and do not assume the older geography rule remains universal. Custom Branding remains 50 GBP per active month, but May says name appears on new mandates five business days after request, while November says activation typically takes ten business days and new mandates after activation show the name (old raw lines 200-214; new raw lines 304-308).

November Billing retries section no longer labels the feature private preview and now bounds automatic insufficient-funds retries to two within 30 days, with no debit-failure fee for Stripe-initiated retries (new raw lines 310-316); May labeled Direct Debit retries private preview without a count (old raw lines 216-218). The new support matrix also marks recurring and PaymentIntents with setup_future_usage supported, but SetupIntents and off-session payments unsupported (new raw lines 210-247); existing concept stripe-bacs-direct-debit line 82 describes a dated Checkout setup_future_usage: off_session route. These statements should be reported in their exact API/UI scope, without inferring that recurring Bacs has been deprecated or that a SetupIntent is possible through Payment Element.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bacs-debit, the November guide describes reusable, delayed GBP debits from UK bank accounts for businesses in its broad supported-country list, subject to Bacs access/identity checks, a customer Direct Debit Instruction mandate, and a default 10,000 GBP per-transaction limit; new users also have a distinct 10,000 GBP weekly limit (new raw lines 5-31, 65-85, 156-184). It supports recurring payments but marks specific off-session and SetupIntent API paths unsupported, while Checkout setup mode is given for collecting details; custom API mandate collection needs separate Stripe approval (new raw lines 164-170, 210-247). Bacs requires collection/confirmation and advance-debit notices; Stripe emails these by default except for enterprise accounts with a custom SUN, and merchant-sent notices follow eligibility and approval (new raw lines 298-302). An existing-mandate debit typically confirms in four business days, a new-mandate debit up to seven; Checkout submission, mandate notices and PaymentIntent processing are not payment success, and T+3 success differs from T+4 funds availability (new raw lines 259-296, 344-358). May described UK merchant accounts and a 100,000 GBP transaction limit and gave the automatic-email default without the SUN exception (old raw lines 8-14, 102-179). source-stripe-bacs-direct-debit.md retains that dated May scope/limit, five-day branding and unqualified auto-email claim at lines 13-37, requiring reciprocal November correction.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bacs-debit, the November country/MCC and product tables and reorganized headings include real changes in supported merchant locations, a 10,000 GBP default transaction limit versus May 100,000 GBP, typical Custom Branding activation of ten versus five business days, more explicit custom-mandate approval, refund outcome, one-dispute/no-evidence rules, bounded insufficient-funds retries and the enterprise custom-SUN exception to default Stripe debit emails (new raw lines 22-85, 130-208, 298-316; old raw lines 8-12, 127-179, 200-218). source-stripe-bacs-direct-debit.md must preserve May provenance and date its UK-only, limit, Connect, retry and blanket auto-email claims while adding the new capture and canonical URL (source lines 1-41). Bacs still requires notices; self-sent notices need eligibility/approval, and the SUN exception does not imply universal suppression (new raw lines 298-302). Pay by Bank Recurring remains a separate private preview (new raw lines 197-208). The new off-session/SetupIntent matrix needs qualification beside its recurring/setup_future_usage and Checkout setup-mode statements (new raw lines 164-168, 210-247). Checkout session.completed, mandate/setup confirmation, refund.created and an estimated debit date do not prove final payment, refund posting or available funds; use integration-specific success/failure events and Refund status (new raw lines 130-134, 259-296, 344-358).
